Resolved by evidence, not by a different model. Part 10b: $6ca9 is the state whose handler last ran, stamped at handler entry ($f5e2 writes 1, $f7f6 writes 2, $1094a writes $14, $109aa writes $15, $f1c0 clears it). Not a facing flag. disc-core writes it from the handler now and the row passes for the right reason.

Part 10e: the writer is $14bb8, the tile-collapse effect. $a3a6 (lea $7656 = $7616 + 8 cells) shows cells 1..8 and 9..16 are the same eight tiles -- 1..8 the record the damage path writes, 9..16 the copy the movement code reads. Destroying a low cell claims the single effect slot at $779e, runs 48 frames off the $5be4 list, and the tick after clears the HIGH copy's type only, which is the (1,1)->(0,1) the fixture reads. disc-core models it as tile::Collapse and tile_damage.ndjson now runs 214/214 clean.

Part 10g: the dwell was a caught disc. --watch on $6e4e gives all four writers of disc+$10: $a9b8 (st, the serve claims the slot), $caae/$cb1e (addq.b #4, player 2 catches it from state 18 or 27), $a570 (addq.b #4, the round ended), and $012588 (subq.b #1, the RENDER pass counting a retired slot down -- which is why reading $a4ea never found it). $ff+4 = $03 and the first countdown step lands in the same tick as the catch, so a caught disc reads 2,1,0 and never moves again. disc-core models all four and discs[n].active is a COMPARED row; both fixtures stay clean.
